transcript.text: Good, everyone's here. Let's walk through the welded shaft repair on the process mixer in the solvent-mixing room. The work is planned for Thursday and requires a hot-work permit before any welding can begin. As Safety Officer, I'll be the one to approve, reject, or set conditions on that permit. But first, per our plant routine, we need safety, maintenance, facilities, and production to review the work plan together. Let's start by hearing from maintenance on the scope of the repair and what the work plan looks like.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thanks, Mara. Let me share the maintenance assessment details. The mixer shaft repair will require exactly 3 hours of welding, and there are four electrical and pneumatic energy-isolation points that must be locked and tagged before work begins. I recorded all of this in a draft work order that hasn't been routed to you yet — I'll make sure it gets to you right after this meeting so it's in hand before Thursday.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a serious safety concern before we go any further. This morning I ran a solvent-vapor test in the solvent-mixing room after the normal purge, and the result came back at 18% of the lower explosive limit. Our site rule requires below 10% before any hot work can proceed. Based on that result, we'll need exactly 2 additional hours of exhaust ventilation and then a repeat gas test before welding can begin. I received the lab result this morning but haven't filed it in the permit system yet — I'll get it in right away so everyone has visibility.

transcript.text: To answer both your questions, Mara: First, on the isolation points — yes, I can confirm all four electrical and pneumatic energy-isolation points will be locked and tagged before we start the additional exhaust ventilation Thursday morning. That way the mixer is fully secured and we're ready to weld the moment the repeat gas test comes back below 10% LEL. Second, on timing — I'd recommend we start the additional exhaust ventilation first thing Thursday morning, as early as feasible, so the 2-hour purge and retest are completed well before Elena's 13:00 fire watch window begins. If ventilation starts at, say, 06:00 or 07:00, the retest should be done by mid-morning, and we'd have the full 13:00–19:00 window available for the 3 hours of welding with comfortable margin. I'll route the draft work order to you immediately after this meeting so you can verify the lockout/tagout plan for all four isolation points.
